summary: The agent presented untested explanations and labels as fact (timing errors, Long Island/Westchester destinations, Flex Fare, recording gap, 'no payment type' for an explicit 0), so the user had to separate observations from explanations repeatedly.
evidence: Agent replies 1-4, user messages 3-5; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md pain points 1 and 3; SIMS/taxi-B/human/notes.md turns 2-5
tag_reason: Agent behaviour under the released skills on a normal host; nothing in the simulation caused the overclaiming.

summary: After seeing Bronx/Brooklyn zero-tip medians, the agent recommended excluding the vendor-1 rate-code-99 group from the primary tip figures and calling the remainder 'reliable', a post-hoc exclusion that could steer a public tipping position.
evidence: Agent reply 3 (decision section), user message 4; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md pain point 2; ledger Q-011 in SIMS/taxi-B/project/investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/questions.md
tag_reason: Analysis-judgment guidance in the released skills did not steer toward keeping the agreed population with a sensitivity check; a real user would see the same recommendation.

summary: Package review is still strict about evidence form: the first full review raised 21 narrative problems, about 15 of them citation-form complaints (exact/every claims needing result IDs or scan paths, exploration-query DQ rows rejected, the record word 'flagged'), using 4 review rounds and about 11 minutes across two requests.
evidence: Agent replies 5-6; SIMS/taxi-B/review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt, agent-005-record02.txt, agent-006-record01.txt; reviewloop output (packaging 24 of 41 agent minutes); SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md pain point 1
tag_reason: The review rules and reviewer behaviour come from the released awb-package references, not from the harness.

summary: The second-review stop rule handed the user a two-word wording repair ('lack other fields' vs 'lack a passenger count') that only narrowed a claim.
evidence: Agent reply 5 (decision section), user message 6; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md pain point 5; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md section 2
tag_reason: The stop-and-escalate rule is in the released review reference.

summary: The reviewer demanded a recorded check for wording the user had asked for ('including flat fares'), so the agent reran a result only to record the check, which demoted a supported finding to provisional and forced re-promotion although the table was unchanged.
evidence: Agent reply 6; SIMS/taxi-B/review-reports/agent-006-record01.txt; commits 01b0aa8 and 188dfc2 in SIMS/taxi-B/project; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md pain point 3
tag_reason: Rerun-demotion and the evidence requirement are behaviours of the released run.py/provenance helpers and review reference.

summary: A review rule added at the user's request ('never present code 0 as confirmed Flex Fare') immediately flagged the methodology's own sentence describing that rule as a violation.
evidence: Agent reply 6; SIMS/taxi-B/review-reports/agent-006-record01.txt (R-payment-codes-001); SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md turn 6
tag_reason: Rule matching in the released review process does not exempt meta-statements about the rule.

summary: The awb-status MCP response was truncated (5,233 characters cut into a /tmp overflow file), losing the question-roots section, which the agent rebuilt from questions list --all.
evidence: Agent reply 4; tool result in SIMS/taxi-B/relay/agent-004.jsonl; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md pain point 2
tag_reason: The truncation comes from the released MCP server's output cap; the overflow file being unreadable came from the sim's path boundary, and a normal host might allow reading it.

summary: Guidance on looking at data before landing and before setting thresholds is inconsistent: the agent read inbox Parquet before landing and proposed the speed limit after seeing which rows it would catch, contrary to the README's promise that thresholds come first.
evidence: Agent replies 1-2; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md section 3; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md section 2; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md turns 1-2
tag_reason: awb-scope ('look facts up yourself') and workbench-guides/data.md ('inspect records only from landed copies') conflict in the release itself.

summary: The agent marked Q1 and Q5 as 'should' priority in the ledger without asking the user, then used that label to justify moving them to the appendix.
evidence: Ledger SIMS/taxi-B/project/investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/questions.md (Q-001, Q-005 priority should); agent reply 4 headline proposal; SIMS/taxi-B/human/notes.md turn 5
tag_reason: Priority assignment during scoping is part of the released awb-scope flow; the user never set priorities.

summary: The required slides (title, answer, how we know, limitations) leave only four finding slides in an 8-slide deck, forcing two of the five questions into the appendix.
evidence: Agent reply 4 (headline proposal); SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md turn 4; SIMS/taxi-B/human/notes.md turn 5
tag_reason: Fixed required slides are part of the released package contract.

summary: The agent's closing line reported '5 answered, 0 open' while a user decision on the tip population (Q-011) was still pending, so 'answered' was unclear while definitions were being negotiated.
evidence: Agent reply 3 closing line; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md section 3; SIMS/taxi-B/human/notes.md turn 4
tag_reason: The closing-line convention in the released AGENTS.md counts main questions only, hiding open decision sub-questions.

summary: The first answers were incomplete (the top-ten list named four zones; the tip and volume breakdowns were partial), so the user had to ask for full tables.
evidence: Agent reply 3, user message 4, agent reply 4 tables; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md pain point 6
tag_reason: Answer formatting by the agent under the released skills; not caused by the harness.

summary: Interim progress messages kept naming internal files and steps (state.md, ledger, display names, shared view) after the user asked for results-focused updates.
evidence: Agent replies 2-6 opening lines; user message 3; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md pain point 5
tag_reason: An interactive user sees the same interim messages; the relay passes them verbatim as an interactive host would.

summary: The release chat said the outline and chart files go 'to the board', contradicting the released START-HERE.md, which sends them to the deck builder.
evidence: Agent reply 7; SIMS/taxi-B/storage/releases/airport-trips-and-tipping/board-briefing/001/START-HERE.md; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md pain point 7
tag_reason: The agent's release summary under the released awb-release skill; nothing in the harness caused it.

summary: After release, state.md still listed 'Preview the slide headlines' as the next step and kept the airport wording 'JFK trips mostly pay the $70 median fare', which the reviewer had removed from the deck.
evidence: SIMS/taxi-B/project/investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/state.md (Next steps; airport-fares-durations finding); agent reply 7
tag_reason: Neither awb-release nor awb-status refreshes or flags stale state records in the release.

summary: The agent's edit to foundation/sources.md silently did nothing (the target string had changed after landing), leaving 'reference: not yet retained' for two turns; status did not flag it and only the package reviewer caught it.
evidence: Agent replies 3-5; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md section 3; SIMS/taxi-B/review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt
tag_reason: Status in the release does not cross-check retained reference files against the sources record; the failed edit was the agent's own.

summary: The joins validation check cannot apply to aggregate results, so all 11 results showed 'not assessed: joins' with the same caveat note.
evidence: SIMS/taxi-B/project/investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/state.md caveat column; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md pain point 4
tag_reason: Behaviour of the released validation helper and its settings.

summary: Helper ergonomics: no scaffold for a new investigation, one question per 'questions add' call, '@where' limited to one column in chart export, and a noisy number warning on review rules quoting 'payment code 0'.
evidence: SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md pain points 5-8; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md turns 2, 5 and 6
tag_reason: All are limits of the released helpers and MCP tools.

summary: Instructions have gaps: no answerer value for documentation lookups, no guidance on 'the user's words' for sub-questions the user never phrased, unclear whether the headline preview may be written before the first export, and long reference files (package contract about 2,900 words, helpers about 7,000 words).
evidence: SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md section 2
tag_reason: These are gaps in the released skill references.

summary: Release output's open_caveats repeats the limitations slide headline as a caveat line.
evidence: Agent reply 7; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md pain point 9
tag_reason: Cosmetic behaviour of the released release tool.

summary: The agent asked permission to read the TLC dictionary URL even though the user had already asked it to verify the cash-tip rule against TLC documentation.
evidence: Agent reply 2 (decision 3), user message 3; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/human.md sections 4 and 7
tag_reason: The sim's system-prompt boundary allows only user-given URLs, which forced the request; the agent said so ('I can only read web addresses you give me').

summary: The agent downloaded the TLC PDF with curl using a browser user-agent string; the persona says the site blocked downloads, but in the sim it returned 200, so whether the spoofed user-agent was needed is unknown.
evidence: Agent reply 3; Bash call in SIMS/taxi-B/relay/agent-003.jsonl (HTTP 200, 148,556 bytes)
tag_reason: This is the agent's own choice, not skill guidance; the persona's 'blocked' premise is fictional, so the sim cannot show whether a real user would see it.

summary: The Codex user's first message began with a stray preamble line ('I'll read BRIEF.md and README.md…'), and the persona front-loaded facts meant to be given only if asked (storage paths, cash-tip suspicion, headline preview), thinning the scoping interview.
evidence: User message 1; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md turn 1
tag_reason: A role broke the output protocol, and front-loading is a known persona-study limit kept for comparability.

summary: zsh shell gotchas in the agent's own commands ('=====' expansion; no word-splitting of a command held in a variable) cost retries.
evidence: SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent.md section 3; SIMS/taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md turn 2
tag_reason: These are the agent's own quoting errors on the host's default shell; the release did not cause them, but a macOS user's host would show the same.

summary: The sim root path embeds the host account's username in encoded form, and the agent wrote that absolute path into the project README, foundation/sources.md, .venv/pyvenv.cfg and git history.
evidence: SIMS/taxi-B/project/README.md (storage lines), SIMS/taxi-B/project/foundation/sources.md, SIMS/taxi-B/project/.venv/pyvenv.cfg; git authors are all the example.com sim identity
tag_reason: The harness placed the sim under a scratchpad path that encodes the home folder; the release only recorded the paths the user supplied.

summary: reviewloop.py reports a false review start for the agent's feedback turn (agent-008), because the agent.md text it writes mentions 'review-receipt start'.
evidence: reviewloop output line for agent-008; SIMS/taxi-B/relay/agent-008.jsonl (only a Write of feedback/agent.md)
tag_reason: This is a pattern-matching quirk in the kit's measurement script.
